context: The original array is nums = [1, 0, 1, 2, 0, 4, 0, 2, 2, 4] (indices 0 through 9). Values range from 0 through 4, and their frequencies are counter = [3, 2, 3, 0, 2].

Accumulating counter gives the initial prefix = [3, 5, 8, 8, 10]. Initially, prefix[num] counts all elements less than or equal to num. For each num present, prefix[num] - 1 gives its last destination index in res. The figure calls these sums prefix. The code in the text accumulates and stores them directly in counter.
The result array res has ten slots. Unwritten slots are drawn blank to distinguish them from slots that already hold the value 0, even though the code initializes res with zeros.
description: Scan nums from right to left. Write the current value num into res[prefix[num] − 1], then decrease prefix[num] by 1. If another copy of the value remains, the updated prefix[num] − 1 gives its next destination index. Thus prefix changes with each write and no longer holds the original prefix sums.

Scanning backward and filling from right to left work together: the rightmost of two equal elements is placed first, farther right in its result segment, and the leftmost is placed later, farther left. This preserves stability. The first four writes shown use original indices 9, 8, 7, and 6. The figure skips the six intervening writes, shows the completed traversal, and finally copies res back into nums.

frames.announcement: The counts are three 0s, two 1s, three 2s, no 3s, and two 4s.
frames.explanation: Scan the original array nums and count the occurrences of 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4. This gives the length-5 count array counter = [3, 2, 3, 0, 2]. No prefix sums have been computed and no result slots have been written.

state_tables.caption: Counting sort step 1: frequencies in counter

frames.title: Count the frequencies

frames.announcement: Accumulate the frequencies in prefix to find the last writable index in res for each value present.
frames.explanation: Accumulate counter to get prefix = [3, 5, 8, 8, 10], and prepare ten empty slots in res. From prefix[num] - 1, the last destination for 0 is 3 - 1 = 2, for 2 it is 8 - 1 = 7, and for 4 it is 10 - 1 = 9. Since 3 never occurs, it triggers no write.
frames.key_state: The prefix sums are prefix = [3, 5, 8, 8, 10]. No elements have been written to res.

frames.title: Accumulate the frequencies and prepare the result array

frames.announcement: Read 4 from original index 9, moving right to left. Write it at result index 9 and decrease prefix[4] by 1.
frames.explanation: The pointer num is at original index 9, the rightmost position, which holds 4. Before decrementing, prefix[4] = 10, so the destination is 10 - 1 = 9. Write 4 to res[9], then decrement prefix[4] by 1 to 9. The figure shows prefix after the decrement. Only original index 9 has been processed, leaving nine slots unwritten.
frames.key_state: The 4 from original index 9 is in res[9] = 4, and prefix[4] has decreased to 9. Nine slots remain unwritten.

frames.explanation: The pointer num moves left to original index 8, which holds 2. Before decrementing, prefix[2] = 8, so the destination is 8 - 1 = 7. Write 2 to res[7], then decrement prefix[2] by 1 to 7. The figure shows prefix after the decrement. Original indices 9 down through 8 have been processed.
frames.key_state: The 2 from original index 8 is in res[7] = 2, and prefix[2] has decreased to 7. Original indices 9 down through 8 have been processed.

frames.announcement: Read 2 from original index 7, write it at result index 6, and decrease prefix[2] by 1.
frames.explanation: The pointer num moves left to original index 7 and finds another 2. The previous decrement left prefix[2] = 7, so the destination is 7 - 1 = 6. Write this 2 to res[6], just left of the previous 2, preserving their original order. Then decrement prefix[2] by 1 to 6. Original indices 9 down through 7 have been processed.
frames.key_state: The 2 from original index 7 is in res[6] = 2, and prefix[2] has decreased to 6. Original indices 9 down through 7 have been processed.

frames.announcement: Read 0 from original index 6, write it at result index 2, and decrease prefix[0] by 1.
frames.explanation: The pointer num moves left to original index 6, which holds 0. Before decrementing, prefix[0] = 3, so the destination is 3 - 1 = 2. Write 0 to res[2], then decrement prefix[0] by 1 to 2. The figure shows prefix after the decrement. Original indices 9 down through 6 have been processed. The zero in res[2] has actually been written. “Unwritten” means that no element has been placed there yet.
frames.key_state: The 0 from original index 6 is in res[2] = 0, and prefix[0] has decreased to 2. Original indices 9 down through 6 have been processed.

frames.announcement: The remaining six backward writes are complete, and the result array res is fully sorted.
frames.explanation: Continue backward from original index 5 through 0. Write the six values 4, 0, 2, 1, 0, 1 to indices 8, 1, 5, 4, 0, 3 of res, respectively. The figure skips these six intermediate frames and goes straight to the end of the scan. The sorted sequence fills res, while the original array nums above still awaits the copy.
frames.key_state: The complete ascending sequence fills res. The elements of nums are still in their original order.

frames.title: Complete the remaining six writes

frames.announcement: Copy the sorted result res back into the original array nums to finish counting sort.
frames.explanation: Finally, copy the ten sorted elements from res to the same indices in nums. The upper array becomes [0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 4, 4], completing counting sort. Now prefix = [0, 3, 5, 8, 8]. For the values present, 0, 1, 2, and 4, the entries are their first indices in res: 0, 3, 5, and 8, respectively. Since 3 is absent, prefix[3] = 8 does not point to a 3. It equals the starting index for 4. Each final prefix[num] counts the input elements smaller than num. For example, 8 elements are smaller than 3, so even the absent value 3 has an entry of 8.
frames.key_state: The result in res has been copied back into nums, completing counting sort.

summary: Accumulate the frequencies into prefix sums to find destination indices. Scan the input backward, writing to res and decrementing the counts, then copy the result back into nums.
title: Stable placement in counting sort using prefix sums
